title: Agent Control Fail-Closed Readiness
dataSources: Agent responses and traces for controlled steps during a control-server outage test
description: Plans for the Agent Control server being unreachable. Calls to controlled steps are blocked when the server cannot be reached, so control-server availability becomes agent availability.
value: A team that expects controls to fail open finds its agent down during a control server outage. Knowing the behaviour up front means the outage is handled in the app and in the runbook.
implementation: Treat the control server as a dependency of the agent. In a test environment, make the server unreachable and confirm controlled steps are blocked and the app returns a clear message. Add the server to the agent's dependency monitoring and runbook.
visualization: Outage test results; the agent's own availability dashboard listing the control server as a dependency.

references.title: Splunk Agent Observability: Agent Control overview

knownFalsePositives: Blocks during a planned control-server maintenance window are expected; announce the window to the agent's users.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback). Agent Control is a separate server and a separate install (`agent-control-sdk`, plus `agent-control-evaluators`; one of those packages is still named `agent-control-evaluator-galileo`, the platform's old name).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The app calls `agent_control.init` and decorates the step with `@control(step_name=...)`. There are two ways to bind a control, and a tenant uses one of them. The Splunk Agent Observability docs pass the resolved `agent_stream_id` (not the stream name) as `target_id` and attach the control to the stream in the console. The SDK path calls `init(agent_name=...)`, creates a policy, adds the control to it, and assigns the policy to that agent name. If the repo already has an example, follow it. Run the decorated step inside an open trace so the control span lands on that trace.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

A control has a scope (step type `llm` or `tool`, step name, and stage `pre` or `post`), a condition (a selector path such as `input` or `output` plus a check from the control server's catalog: regex, list, JSON, SQL, Luna-2 or custom), and an action. Actions, strictest first: deny, steer, observe; deny wins over steer over observe. Regex patterns are RE2, so there is no lookahead. Write the pattern as the thing to catch: the engine has no "unless".

Step 3 — Validate

Run the outage test in a test environment and record which steps were blocked and what the user saw. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Repeat the test after Agent Control upgrades and after adding a control to a new step.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Steps not blocked during the test: they are not decorated with `@control()`, so no control applies to them.
grandmaExplanation: If the guard's office is closed, the guarded doors stay locked, so we plan for the office being closed.

productArtifacts.title: Fail-closed readiness test
productArtifacts.body:
Behaviour: if the control server cannot be reached, the call is blocked.
Test: in a test environment, make the control server unreachable and call each controlled step.
Expect: the step is blocked; the app returns a clear message and the trace records the failure.
Runbook: list the control server as an agent dependency, with owner and escalation.
Do not claim: how long a control check takes; the documentation does not say.
